# THE TORUS ATLAS

*What the sea is for: a live sailable chart, kept beside the Atlas rather than inside it.*

---

## I. WHAT IT IS

The Atlas derives the plane: two integers, twenty-seven stars cut from open
water, the modular group as the torus's own shear, the found radius at root
two. This instrument sails that plane instead of only deriving it. The
twenty-seven cards render as a glyph cluster set on a live torus, each
glyph's size and depth carrying its own weight in the ladder rather than a
flat list order, turning under a play control so the same coordinate system
can be watched rather than only read.

The live surface: [the sea](/app/luminara-sea.html).

## II. WHAT IT IS NOT

Not a second derivation. Every claim about why the plane is shaped this way
belongs to the Atlas; this card exists only to give the instrument built on
top of it a shelf of its own. Not yet in the main navigation either: the sea
remains a workshop surface until the architect graduates it, so what a
visitor finds there today may still be in motion.

---

## PROVENANCE

Named at the architect's word, 2026-07-25. The instrument itself predates
this card considerably; the card's only job is to point.

---

*The plane is derived once. This is where it is sailed.*
